Loss-of-function mutations in SDHB, SDHC, or SDHD impair the function of the succinate dehydrogenase complex (Complex II) in the mitochondrial electron transport chain. This disruption leads to a cascade of cellular events ultimately manifesting as the distinct phenotypes of pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndrome 4 and Carney-Stratakis syndrome, including tumors such as pheochromocytomas, paragangliomas, GISTs, and pulmonary chondromas.

partners.mechanism_chain: SDHB (HGNC:10681) —DISRUPTS→ Succinate Dehydrogenase Activity (GO:0005913); SDHB (HGNC:10681) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial Electron Transport Complex II (GO:0005746); Succinate Dehydrogenase Activity (GO:0005913) —DECREASES→ Succinate (CHEBI:17174); Succinate (CHEBI:17174) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial Electron Transport Complex II (GO:0005746); Mitochondrial Electron Transport Complex II (GO:0005746) —LEADS_TO→ Pheochromocytoma/Paraganglioma (HP:0001727); Mitochondrial Electron Transport Complex II (GO:0005746) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial Complex II Deficiency (HP:0033685). Loss-of-function mutations in SDHB impair the activity of succinate dehydrogenase (Complex II). This leads to reduced function of the mitochondrial electron transport chain and accumulation of succinate. The dysfunction of Complex II directly causes mitochondrial complex 2 deficiency. The accumulation of succinate, a known oncometabolite, is implicated in the development of pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas, potentially through epigenetic modifications or reactive oxygen species production.
